rationale.conceptual: The method (MNDO) is a standard semi-empirical quantum chemistry method implemented in the widely used MOPAC package. Computing vibrational frequencies from optimized geometries via numerical force constants and the GF matrix is a routine workflow. No custom derivations or deep domain tricks are required; the solver needs to understand the tool input and output format, but not create new theory.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of generating 5 simple input files, running MOPAC (one job per molecule), and parsing the output to extract bond lengths and IR-active modes. This is a few‑step process with only one external tool; it can be scripted in a single batch file. No complex environment setup or multi‑tool orchestration is needed.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires running standard MNDO calculations with the MOPAC program on five very small molecules, then extracting bond lengths and IR frequencies. The underlying method is a well-established semi-empirical quantum chemical approach, and the work involves no novel algorithms or complex theory. The pipeline is short and needs only scripting of tool execution and output parsing.

compute_estimate.reasoning: All molecules are extremely small (3–7 atoms) so MNDO runs are lightweight; peak RAM usage is well under 100 MB and there is no external dataset. No GPU is required.
